chunk_findings.detail: The two call sites in this diff show that `O.refused` and `O.failed` are distinct constructors with different shapes. The new refusal site at line ~211 calls `O.refused("companions.added", ..., actions=[], applied=False, written=0, refused=[...])` — i.e. it supplies the refusal fields (`actions`, `applied`, `written`, `refused`) and no `path`/`rows`/`text`. The new branch here instead reuses `O.failed`'s keyword set: `done("config", err, path="", rows=[], text="")`. Since `err` is a `KeyRefused` instance on this branch, and `KeyRefused` is not something `O.failed` would ever be handed, this passes the failed-outcome arguments to the refused-outcome constructor without any of the refusal-specific fields. Concretely, with `ddflow config --append-toml 'a.b = 1'` (or any appended block containing a quoted/dotted/non-ASCII key), `_append_config` returns the `KeyRefused` error, `isinstance(err, KeyRefused)` is true, and this line invokes `O.refused("config", err, path="", rows=[], text="")`, which does not match the `O.refused` signature used elsewhere in the file (unexpected `path`/`rows`/`text`, missing `refused`), so the command raises `TypeError` on the very path this change is supposed to fix instead of returning the plain-key refusal. Contrast this with the companion-id surface added just above, which calls `O.refused` correctly with the refusal fields; the copied `O.failed` argument list was not adapted.

chunk_findings.detail:
The `_TOKEN` string alternatives cannot lex a multi-line string that contains two adjacent quotes, which is legal TOML that `tomllib` accepts (the spec's own example `"""Here are two quotation marks: "". Simple enough."""`). For the inner loop, at the first `"` of `""` the branch `"(?!")` fails (next char is `"`) and `[^"\\]` fails, so `(?:...)*` stops; the closing `"{3,5}` then sees only `""` followed by a non-quote (e.g. `y`) and cannot reach 3 quotes, so the whole `"""..."""` token fails and the region is shred-tokenized. Consecutive newlines inside that shredded value then become `nl` tokens, and the walk's `if kind == "nl": at_key = at_key or not opened` resets `at_key` to `True` (`opened` is empty), so string content is re-interpreted as keys. Concretely, for the perfectly valid TOML

    a = """x
    ""y"""

(a string value equal to `x\n""y`), the tokens become `[word a][=][str ""][word x][nl][str ""][word y][str ""][nl]`; after the stray `nl` sets `at_key=True`, the token `""` enters the `elif at_key and kind in ("word","str")` branch, the loop `while toks[k][1] != "="` scans to the end of the list with no `=`, and `appended_key_problem` raises `IndexError`. With content that does happen to contain a quoted key line (e.g. `a = """\n"b" = 1\n""c"""`), it instead returns a `KeyRefused` for a key that is inside a string, i.e. it falsely refuses valid TOML. The same defect applies to multi-line literal strings containing `''` inside `'''...'''`. This is not an "invalid input" edge case: the function's contract is that the text has already been accepted by `tomllib`, so crashing or refusing on such input is a regression introduced by this tokenizer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:_TOKEN (`appended_key_problem`)

chunk_findings.detail: The second parametrization case is misclassified. `["flow"]` is a quoted table key whose content `flow` is a valid ASCII bare key, so it *does* have a plain spelling — exactly like the case `[gate."unit_tests"]` in the sibling test, which this file asserts must be refused "with the plain spelling otherwise" and whose assertion is `f"use {plain}" in err`. The stated rule ("Every key in an appended block must be a plain dotted ASCII bare key, refused with the plain spelling otherwise") therefore requires the refusal for `["flow"]` to name `flow`, i.e. an error of the `...; use flow` form. But this test asserts `"letters, digits" in err`, i.e. the no-plain-spelling message form used for cases like `[gate."two words"]`. The file's own earlier test (line ~93) establishes that these two refusals are distinct messages: it asserts `"; use " not in err` for a key refused without a plain-spelling suggestion, whereas the naming test asserts the message contains `use <plain>`. So a conforming implementation refuses `["flow"]` with a message naming `flow` and without the `letters, digits` text, making this parametrization fail. Either the case must move to `test_an_appended_block_with_a_quoted_key_is_refused_naming_the_plain_one` with `plain="flow"`, or a genuinely no-plain key must be used here.

chunk_findings.detail: The `KNOB_OUTWARD` table is built as `{ **{key: frozenset() for key in KNOB_CHOICES}, ...overrides }`, so every knob not explicitly listed silently receives an *empty* outward set. The comment directly above it claims this is "so a new knob cannot skip the question," and the docblock claims `tests/test_config_enum_knobs.py` "requires an entry for every `KNOB_CHOICES` key here and in `KNOB_OUTWARD`." Both claims are false in the harmful direction: because the comprehension pre-populates every key, the "has an entry" requirement is vacuously satisfied, and any enforcement test that checks "no `KNOB_STRICTEST` fallback is an outward value" will pass for a knob that is not explicitly listed here. Concrete failure: a future knob `foo` with choices `("local", "remote")` whose `KNOB_STRICTEST` fallback is `"remote"` and which is forgotten in this dict gets `frozenset()` as its outward set; the test sees no outward value and passes, yet a typo in a config file now makes ddflow write remote refs — exactly what D-fallback-no-remote is supposed to forbid. The safety check only holds for knobs someone remembered to enumerate; the auto-fill removes the forcing function the comment asserts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py (KNOB_OUTWARD definition)

chunk_findings.detail: The test no longer independently pins the outward values of any knob other than `flow.integration` and `flow.claims`; the loop iterates over `C.KNOB_OUTWARD` itself, so the table is effectively checked against itself. The removed version hard-coded `flow.pr_merge: {"on_approval", "auto"}` in the test, so an omission in that set was impossible; now only the key-set equality (`set(C.KNOB_OUTWARD) == set(C.KNOB_CHOICES)`) and the two literal asserts remain. Concrete false negative: if `C.KNOB_OUTWARD["flow.pr_merge"]` is `{"on_approval"}` (i.e. `"auto"` dropped) while `KNOB_CHOICES["flow.pr_merge"]` still contains `"auto"` and `C.strictest("flow.pr_merge")` returns `"auto"`, then `values <= set(choices)` holds, `strictest(...) not in values` holds (`"auto" not in {"on_approval"}`), and the test passes — even though the strictest/fallback value enables a forge-side auto-merge, which is exactly the remote/forge interaction this test is documented to forbid. The same omission for any other knob (e.g. `flow.claims`, if the literal assert were ever relaxed) is likewise undetectable, so the test's guarantee reduces to "the two hard-coded entries are correct", not "no strictest value is outward".
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_config_enum_knobs.py:395-399 (test_no_strictest_value_contacts_the_remote_or_the_forge)

chunk_findings.detail: The loop now takes its oracle from `C.KNOB_OUTWARD` — the very table the change is supposed to validate — so for any given knob the only independent check left is the pair of hardcoded assertions, and there are only two of them. `flow.pr_merge` lost the independent expectation it had in the deleted module-level `OUTWARD` table (`{"on_approval", "auto"}`), and the new test never asserts anything about its contents: `set(C.KNOB_OUTWARD) == set(C.KNOB_CHOICES)` only proves the *key* exists, and `values <= set(C.KNOB_CHOICES[key])` / `C.strictest(key) not in values` both read their answer from `C.KNOB_OUTWARD[key]` itself. Concretely, if the production half of this change ships `KNOB_OUTWARD["flow.pr_merge"] = frozenset()` (or `{"off"}`) while `KNOB_STRICTEST["flow.pr_merge"] = "auto"`, this test passes green even though a bad file value for `flow.pr_merge` still turns on forge-side merge — exactly the D-fallback-no-remote failure the test is named for. The same hole applies to any future enum knob whose `KNOB_OUTWARD` entry is recorded as empty/mislabeled: the key-set equality forces the knob to be *listed*, but not to be listed truthfully. The `flow.integration`/`flow.claims` hardcoded asserts cover only those two knobs, so at minimum the `flow.pr_merge` entry (and ideally the mapping from each knob to its outward values) needs an independent expectation rather than a self-read.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_config_enum_knobs.py:390 (test_no_strictest_value_contacts_the_remote_or_the_forge)

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization is self-contradictory: `"flow"` **does** have a plain spelling (`flow`), so it belongs with the "name the plain one" cases in `test_an_appended_block_with_a_quoted_key_is_refused_naming_the_plain_one`, not in the "no plain spelling" case. The sibling test proves the contract for exactly this shape — `('[gate."unit_tests"]\ntimeout_s = 5\n', "gate.unit_tests")` requires the refusal to say `use gate.unit_tests`, i.e. a quoted segment that is a valid bare key is reported by its plain spelling. `["flow"]` is the same construct, so a correct implementation refuses it with `use flow`, and the assertion `"letters, digits" in err` will fail (or, at best, this case silently asserts nothing about the plain-key rule). Either this case should be dropped, or it should be moved into the first parametrization with `plain == "flow"` and asserted as `use flow`.

(a string value equal to `x\n""y`), the tokens become `[word a][=][str ""][word x][nl][str ""][word y][str ""][nl]`; after the stray `nl` sets `at_key=True`, the token `""` enters the `elif at_key and kind in ("word","str")` branch, the loop `while toks[k][1] != "="` scans to the end of the list with no `=`, and `appended_key_problem` raises `IndexError`. With content that does happen to contain a quoted key line (e.g. `a = """\n"b" = 1\n""c"""`), it instead returns a `KeyRefused` for a key that is inside a string, i.e. it falsely refuses valid TOML. The same defect applies to multi-line literal strings containing `''` inside `'''...'''`. This is not an "invalid input" edge case: the function's contract is that the text has already been accepted by `tomllib`, so crashing or refusing on such input is a regression introduced by this tokenizer.

chunk_findings.detail: The second parametrization case is misclassified. `["flow"]` is a quoted table key whose content `flow` is a valid ASCII bare key, so it *does* have a plain spelling — exactly like the case `[gate."unit_tests"]` in the sibling test, which this file asserts must be refused "with the plain spelling otherwise" and whose assertion is `f"use {plain}" in err`. The stated rule ("Every key in an appended block must be a plain dotted ASCII bare key, refused with the plain spelling otherwise") therefore requires the refusal for `["flow"]` to name `flow`, i.e. an error of the `...; use flow` form. But this test asserts `"letters, digits" in err`, i.e. the no-plain-spelling message form used for cases like `[gate."two words"]`. The file's own earlier test (line ~93) establishes that these two refusals are distinct messages: it asserts `"; use " not in err` for a key refused without a plain-spelling suggestion, whereas the naming test asserts the message contains `use <plain>`. So a conforming implementation refuses `["flow"]` with a message naming `flow` and without the `letters, digits` text, making this parametrization fail. Either the case must move to `test_an_appended_block_with_a_quoted_key_is_refused_naming_the_plain_one` with `plain="flow"`, or a genuinely no-plain key must be used here.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new guard for `config --append-toml` only inspects *parsed gate tables* (`_gate_table_problems(result) - _gate_table_problems(_parsed(prev))`). It therefore cannot see a quoted, escaped, or non-ASCII key anywhere else in the appended block, because `tomllib` erases the spelling before the check runs: `[flow]
"tag_prefix" = "v"
` parses to exactly the same dict as `[flow]
tag_prefix = "v"
`, so `Config.check(result)` passes and `_gate_table_problems(result)` returns nothing new (there is no `gate` table). The function then falls through to the success path and appends the block, even though the README text added by this same change promises that `config --append-toml`/`ddflow_configure toml` hold "every key of the block to the same rule — a table header, a key, an inline-table key: `[flow]` then `"tag_prefix" = "v"` is refused with `use flow.tag_prefix`". The same holds for escaped/Unicode spellings (`"tag_prefix"`) and quoted inline-table keys (`thing = { "a b" = 1 }`): after parsing, none are distinguishable from their bare equivalents, and no raw-text tokenization of the block is performed anywhere in the modified path. The two regression tests added in this change only cover dotted `[gate.…]` ids, so the quoted/escaped/non-ASCII half of the stated requirement (bug item 2) is still unenforced and the README contract is false.

prompt = "x"

chunk_findings.detail:
`_bad_values` records *positional* indices into `unknown_knobs`, but nothing keeps those positions valid when `unknown_knobs` later shrinks. The only code that removes entries is `_forget_fallback` (defined immediately below the new method), which runs when a later config layer sets a key that an earlier layer had recorded as a strictest-fallback; it must drop the corresponding `unknown_knobs` entry and re-number the surviving `_fallback_notes` indices so they still index the same strings. `_bad_values` is a new, parallel index list that is never re-numbered there, so its indices become stale (or out of range).

Concrete failure: layer 1 contains `[a] known_enum = "bad"` (a knob in `KNOB_STRICTEST` → fallback note at index 0) and `[a] other_known = "bogus"` (a known knob *not* in `KNOB_STRICTEST` → `_bad_values = [1]`, entry at index 1). Layer 2 sets `[a] known_enum = "good"`, which calls `_forget_fallback`, removes entry 0 from `unknown_knobs` and leaves that list of length 1 while `_bad_values` still holds `1`. Doctor then evaluates `enumerate(config.unknown_knobs)` against `invalid_value_indices()`: index 0 is not in the set, so the real bad-value line is again reported as an unknown config key (exactly the bug Bf3566bbacd is supposed to fix), and if a removal happens *above* the recorded index the stale index silently points at a different entry and the wrong line is labelled "invalid value for …". (A direct `unknown_knobs[i]` lookup would instead raise `IndexError`.) The fix must adjust/remap `_bad_values` in `_forget_fallback`, or store keys rather than positions.
